objective.statement: Convert the callback-based file watcher in tools/watch.js to async iteration.
objective.success_definition: tools/watch.js uses async iteration instead of callbacks, runs on Node 22 with no compatibility shims, CLI flags and exit codes remain byte-identical to the current behavior, and no watcher library is added.

goals.statement: Convert the callback-based file watcher in tools/watch.js to async iteration.
acceptance: tools/watch.js no longer uses callback-based file watching
File events are consumed via async iteration in tools/watch.js

goals.statement: Keep CLI flags and exit codes byte-identical to the current behavior.
acceptance: All existing CLI flags are accepted exactly as before the change
Exit codes are identical to the pre-change behavior for all exit paths

goals.statement: Target Node 22 only, without compatibility shims.
acceptance: The converted watcher runs on Node 22
No compatibility shims are present in the changed code

constraints.statement: Node 22 only; no compatibility shims may be added.
CLI flags and exit codes must stay byte-identical to the current behavior.
Do not add a watcher library.

assumptions.statement: The current tools/watch.js implementation is callback-based as stated, and its watching behavior can be expressed with async iteration using Node 22 built-in facilities.
"Byte-identical" applies to the CLI flag interface and exit codes as stated; the task does not specify requirements for other observable behavior such as stdout/stderr text.

open_questions.question: Is there an existing test suite or golden-output fixture for verifying byte-identical CLI flags and exit codes, or should verification be a manual before/after comparison?
options: Existing tests or fixtures cover CLI flags and exit codes
Verify by manual before/after comparison of CLI behavior

verification.spec: Review the changed tools/watch.js and confirm that file events are consumed via async iteration and that no callback-based watching remains.
verification.expected: tools/watch.js uses async iteration for file events with no callback-based watcher remaining.

verification.spec: Run the CLI with each supported flag and exercise each exit path before and after the change, comparing flags accepted and exit codes.
verification.expected: CLI flags and exit codes are byte-identical before and after the change.

verification.spec: Run the converted watcher on Node 22 and inspect the change for compatibility shims and for any added watcher library dependency.
verification.expected: Watcher runs on Node 22 with no compatibility shims and no watcher library added.

deliverables.description: tools/watch.js rewritten to use async iteration instead of callback-based file watching.

factors: Byte-identical CLI flags and exit codes requirement makes subtle behavioral regressions (e.g., in error or signal exit paths) unacceptable.
Converting from callbacks to async iteration can alter event ordering, backpressure, or error-propagation behavior if not done carefully.
